I'm listening to Morning Phase by Beck right now, and I can't believe how beautiful the sound is. He has really matured as an artist. I always remembered him as this silly, bells-and-whistles style funkadelic beatnik. Now he's playing from this perspective of a sage, like he's very comfortable with warm, simple ambiance and doesn't feel the need to attract attention. I can't say enough good things about this album.

Anyway, the stereotype is that most bands/musicians have a great debut album, then rush out a less-than-great sophomore album in order to cash in on their initial popularity. Then the creativity dies once they hit 30. Are there any other songwriters who kept getting better as they aged?
Voat, what are some musicians who have gotten better with age?

This will probably be an unpopular opinion, but Genesis. The progressive era was undoubtedly good, but I feel like they really belonged when Collins stepped in and turned them into this awesome pop rock group that anyone can appreciate.
Dave Grohl. Nirvana was and always will be great, but the Foo Fighters are even better.
Came here to say Dave Grohl and Foo Fighters. I really liked Sonic Highways and look forward to every album as they get better and better!
I'm not a huge fan of his in FF, although I am think they're good. However, every album he's guest drummed on is amazing.

Good choice with Beck. I'll go with New Order. While I enjoy Joy Division, I feel like the types of songs they would go onto write with New Order are leaps ahead...and catchier. I think 'Regret' is an excellent single and shows even as they neared the end of the 80s they could put something together.
I came here to say Beck, but you beat me to the punch. I guess I'll go with Dinosaur Jr. They've always been awesome, but I think their most recent albums have been top notch.

Taylor Swift. She's gone from teeny bopper to self aware artist with an insanely good voice. I may not like her particular style of music or what she sings about, but god damn does that woman have a voice.

Swans. I love their early no-wave stuff, but their post-reformation output has been on another level. I thought The Seer was one of the best albums of the last decade, then To Be Kind blew it out of the water.

I feel like it's something a lot of us do. Wonder about the meaning to life. Why we are all here. Why some of us have to suffer this illness of depression. I do it. I did it in a session. And you know what my counselor said? She went all Maslow on me.

She pointed out that before I can get to self actualization I need to work through the other steps. At first I thought it was bullshit. But... I know the hierarchy. It kind of makes sense. How could I focus on the purpose of my life when I don't feel as if I belong? I feel some love... sometimes, but there is a huge deficit there that I definitely fixate on. I didn't have all of my safety needs met as a child. Did that fuck me up? I certainly don't have the best self esteem. I have jumped the gun and tried going for the top of the pyramid before figuring out the foundations. I think maybe a lot of other people do the same thing.

For reference, the needs are:

  1. Biological and Physiological needs - air, food, drink, shelter, warmth, sleep.

  2. Safety needs - protection from elements, security, order, law, stability, freedom from fear.

  3. Love and belongingness needs - friendship, intimacy, affection and love, - from work group, family, friends, romantic relationships.

  4. Esteem needs - achievement, mastery, independence, status, dominance, prestige, self-respect, respect from others.

  5. Self-Actualization needs - realizing personal potential, self-fulfillment, seeking personal growth and peak experiences.

Looking at them, there are things in each category that I don't have. So I guess I have a lot of work to do if I want to know what the point is. My next question is... is it worth it?

there's millions of reasons you could feel this way and i'm really sorry you don't feel like you belong anywhere, it must be so hard. whenever i begin asking myself 'is it worth it?' i always look up some inspiring stories from people in similar situations, it makes what i'm going through feel only temporary and that there's a lot in life for you to enjoy

The point is to find a meaning. Doesnt have to be profound or anything that anyone else strive for. Its something that means something for YOU. I've had a lot of issues with depression, and still do depression for me is not something I can get over but just manage. I decided that I dont belong in my country, and Im going to move abroad and thats the best decision for me.

I hope that you can find your own goal and what really means something for you, if you want to ask questions feel free to pm me or reply.
Good luck with moving abroad, I hope you find what you're looking for :)

My next question is... is it worth it?

My best guess is that, yes, it's worth it. I agree with Spectral in that meaning depends on the person. But one conclusion I've come to lately is that rather than find meaning to live - which likely won't come - it's better to assume a priori that life is meaningful. Take it on faith. Why does it make sense to take it on faith? Because depression is a mental illness that influences the way we think. Of course depression is going to tell us that life has no meaning.

Under the assumption that depression compromises your ability to look at things from your own perspective, another thing you can try is to look at things from other people's perspectives. Most people seem to find meaning in life. What do they live for? Maybe a family, or a career. Maybe for experiences, or friendships. Maybe they live to help others.

Anyway this is really just me brainstorming off the top of my head.

My next question is... is it worth it?

It's so hard for me to honestly say yes because I find myself asking the question on a daily basis, but for the sake of hope, I do have to say yes. If you answer no, it's kind of a self fulfilling prophecy, isn't it? If you answer yes, at least there's a glimmer of hope. That's my theory, anyway.

My next question is... is it worth it?

Well, it's not going to feel worth it all the time. It is worth it though, different reasons for different people. Not sure if Maslow is really the answer, but hey, it might be. For me it was family, for you it might be slam poetry. shrug
I think the whole Maslow thing isn't the answer, it just sort of opened my eyes.
